live_web_research.page_text: [2610.12457] SpatialHarness: Test-Time Spatial Scaffolding for Fine Robotic Manipulation Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Robotics arXiv:2610.12457 (cs) [Submitted on 8 Oct 2026] Title: SpatialHarness: Test-Time Spatial Scaffolding for Fine Robotic Manipulation Authors: Jiayu Wang , Yue Yu , Bin Zhu , Zhiyao Yang , Jingjing Chen View a PDF of the paper titled SpatialHarness: Test-Time Spatial Scaffolding for Fine Robotic Manipulation, by Jiayu Wang and 4 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Frontier multimodal foundation models (e.g., GPT-6 Astra) have recently shown strong potential for direct robotic control, yet their performance on fine manipulation remains limited. We argue that an important source of failure is not necessarily insufficient policy capability, but insufficient spatial observability, where task-critical spatial relationships may be poorly revealed by the existing physical camera setup. We introduce SpatialHarness, a test-time embodied harness that provides test-time spatial scaffolding for fine robotic manipulation without policy fine-tuning or changes to the physical sensing setup. SpatialHarness maintains an online simulated scene synchronized with real-world execution, identifies task-critical spatial relationships, and renders complementary virtual views that expose them to a frozen multimodal policy. To keep the simulated scene aligned during interaction, we develop interaction-aware scene synchronization that distinguishes static, held, and transition modes. We evaluate SpatialHarness on four real-robot manipulation tasks spanning precise geometric alignment, object-relative placement, and articulated-object interaction. Using the same frozen GPT-6 Astra policy, SpatialHarness substantially improves task success, including from 26.7% to 66.7% on plug insertion and from 0% to 100% on Tower of Hanoi. These results indicate that improving spatial observability at test time can unlock fine-manipulation capabilities already present in strong multimodal foundation models. Abstract Frontier multimodal foundation models (e.g., GPT-6 Astra) have recently shown strong potential for direct robotic control, yet their performance on fine manipulation remains limited. We argue that an important source of failure is not necessarily insufficient policy capability, but insufficient spatial observability, where task-critical spatial relationships may be poorly revealed by the existing physical camera setup. We introduce SpatialHarness, a test-time embodied harness that provides test-time spatial scaffolding for fine robotic manipulation without policy fine-tuning or changes to the physical sensing setup. SpatialHarness maintains an online simulated scene synchronized with real-world execution, identifies task-critical spatial relationships, and renders complementary virtual views that expose them to a frozen multimodal policy. To keep the simulated scene aligned during interaction, we develop interaction-aware scene synchronization that distinguishes static, held, and transition modes. We evaluate SpatialHarness on four real-robot manipulation tasks spanning precise geometric alignment, object-relative placement, and articulated-object interaction. Using the same frozen GPT-6 Astra policy, SpatialHarness substantially improves task success, including from 26.7% to 66.7% on plug insertion and from 0% to 100% on Tower of Hanoi. These results indicate that improving spatial observability at test time can unlock fine-manipulation capabilities already present in strong multimodal foundation models. Project website: https://emilia113.github.io/SpatialHarness/. Summary SpatialHarness improves fine robotic manipulation by providing test-time spatial scaffolding through synchronized virtual views, enhancing the observability of frozen multimodal foundation models. selected_records.title: SpatialHarness: Test-Time Spatial Scaffolding for Fine Robotic Manipulation

article.body:
SpatialHarness: A Test-Time Spatial Scaffolding Framework for Fine Robotic Manipulation

The research paper "SpatialHarness: Test-Time Spatial Scaffolding for Fine Robotic Manipulation" introduces a framework that enhances the observability of multimodal foundation models for fine manipulation. The framework, SpatialHarness, provides test-time spatial scaffolding without requiring policy fine-tuning or physical hardware changes.

The robot embodiment is not specified in the provided research. The task involves fine robotic manipulation, as the paper focuses on improving the performance of multimodal foundation models on such tasks. The training approach is not explicitly stated, but it appears to involve the use of a frozen GPT-6 Astra policy. The autonomy level is not specified, but the paper discusses test-time spatial scaffolding, suggesting that the robot is operating under some level of autonomy.

The paper was published on arXiv, a preprint server for scientific papers, but no specific date or journal is provided. The research is relevant to the field of robotics and machine learning, particularly in the areas of robotics control and artificial intelligence.
